theme.title: Rotation: Growth → Value & Defensives
theme.summary: Energy (+1.58%) and Health Care (+1.56%) led the market today, while Technology (-2.41%) and Industrials (-1.76%) brought up the rear. That split lines up with a rotation out of growth: growth-oriented sectors averaged -1.13% versus +0.77% for defensives and -0.23% for value and cyclicals, suggesting money moved from high-multiple names into steadier, cash-generative businesses. That shows up at the index level too: the blue-chip Dow gained -0.22% while the tech-heavy Nasdaq fell -1.33%, a wide enough gap to matter. Small caps underperformed as well, with the Russell 2000 at -1.30%, hinting the move favored large, established balance sheets over smaller, more rate-sensitive companies. The VIX rose 4.28% to 15.84, pointing to a bit more caution creeping in beneath the surface. Gold slipped 1.32% to $4,389.50, crude oil was little changed at $84.42, and bitcoin gained 0.15% — cross-asset moves weren't all pointing the same direction as equities.
